nA1.text: Sign in: the Sign in button is a real submit (Enter in any field submits). Errors appear only after submitting. A non-active account gets exactly the 401 “details not recognised” copy, and the 423 copy never names the account or an unlock time.

nA2.text: Focus: on 401 the alert (tabindex -1) takes focus and no field is marked, so the page never reveals which one was wrong. On 403 “code needed” focus moves to the code field, whose error sets aria-invalid.

nA3.text: Order: POST /v1/auth/totp/enroll returns the provisioning link; the QR code and the manual key come from it. POST /v1/auth/totp/verify confirms the code and the account becomes active. No recovery codes are shown or kept (owner decision); the enrolment response still returns them today, so it is tagged Needs API.

nA4.text: The high-severity alert is role=status: it never moves focus and plays no sound. System banners sit above the app bar and the panes shrink to fit; the page still never scrolls.

nA5.text: On load, focus moves to the app bar heading “No permission”. The panel is plain content, not an alert.

nA6.text: Revoke first checks mfa_verified_at. Older than 12 hours: Confirm it’s you opens in the panel beside the scan, then the revoke panel. Fresher: straight to the revoke panel. The session-expired sign-in (to the left) is the only dialog left on this canvas.

nB1.text: Rows: role=row in a body rowgroup; roving tabindex and the focus ring sit on the active gridcell (LyteNyte default). The restaurant name is a real link; Enter opens the application in panes. Fixed order, oldest first: no sortable headers, so no aria-sort. Rows virtualise inside the grid and the next 25 load as you scroll, with a status line. Time left in grid cells is plain text refreshed silently, never a live region; only your own claim strip announces. Dates show short, with the full date in the tooltip and to screen readers.

nB2.text: POST take-next returned data: null while rows were visible (all claimed by others or with their restaurant). The status message takes no focus. When you already hold a claim, the page leads with “Continue review” and Take next is secondary (Queue-TakeHeld).

nC1.text: The halal certificate is never approved or rejected as a document. The client never calls the document review for HALAL_CERTIFICATE; its row and panel only route to the verification console. With no certificate record at all, the row says so and no badge shows (App-NoCertificate).

nC2.text: Panes: the list collapses to a strip, then the application, the documents and the scan. Each document row header is a button (“Review Food safety certificate, version 1”); Enter or Space loads it in the scan pane and moves focus to the review heading. Nothing is preselected in the per-type checklist. Only a pane’s own content scrolls.

nC3.text: The DS Button can’t take aria-describedby yet (proposed enhancement), so the reason is part of the name: “Approve…, unavailable: 2 things stop approval”. Unrecognised blockers read “Another rule stops approval (code: …). Ask engineering to add it to this page.”

nC4.text: Refusals of the application decision, one per board, each a single blocking alert that takes focus above the panes, which shrink to fit. Approval refused because something stops approval: the itemised list, claim still held (App-Blocked). Already decided: the application shows the decision on record (App-Blocked-Decided). Claim ended: the claim strip shows it ended and every decision button is off (App-Blocked-ClaimLost).

nC5.text: Decision records (decided_at, decided_by, reason) are not on RestaurantApplication yet: tagged Needs API. Reversal applies to rejections only, super admin, within 30 days.

nC6.text: Overview beside detail: opening the applications list collapses the scan to a strip so nothing gets narrower than it can work. Opening an application from this list only inspects it; Take next is the only way to claim.

nC7.text: Decisions open in an in-page panel in place of the scan, with the application and documents still in view. Its heading takes focus; Close or Escape returns focus to the button that opened it, and nothing is sent until the panel’s own primary button.

nD1.text: Three panes, one save each: the scan; step 1, the transcription beside the application’s own facts; step 2, all seven checks (SevenChecks); step 3, the decision bar docked under them. The application, the certificate and the seven checks are all in view without scrolling.

nD10.text: Dates valid (H5) copy: the minimum comes from a setting (30 days by default) and the days left from the expiry date against today. Staff never see field names: “Expires 14 October 2026, 16 days from today. Approval needs at least 30 days left. No one can override it.”

nD11.text: After Reject certificate: the neutral toast, then focus on the “still needs a decision” alert. Request changes… opens the application’s request with Halal certificate ticked under documents to redo (a reviewer action they can undo, not a consent). The claim stays held until 2:48 pm.

nD12.text: The application facts beside the transcription always read GET /restaurant-applications/{restaurantId} for the certificate’s restaurant: here Zaytoun Grill’s legal name, display name and address, never another restaurant’s.

nD13.text: Transcription refused for empty fields: count and list every empty required field (7 here, the certified address and dates included), mark each one, and move focus to the first invalid field. The summary alert is role=status so it doesn’t take focus from the field.

nD14.text: 422 CHECK_FAILED: the server recomputes Dates valid (H5) and Unique, not reused (H7) when Approve is pressed. The alert names the failed checks, takes focus, and the checks refetch so Dates valid (H5) shows its computed Fail. Distinct from 422 CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE (Verify-Incomplete).

nD15.text: Each computed or locked Fail has its own reject panel: Dates valid (H5) preselects Expired or expiring, Unique, not reused (H7) preselects Already used by another restaurant, Issuer accepted (H2) preselects Issuer not accepted. The decision bar, the computed-fail alert link and the 422 CHECK_FAILED alert all open these. The panel takes the transcription’s place so the scan and the checks stay in view.

nD16.text: Issuer accepted (H2) and Scope sufficient (H6) restricted rows: SevenChecks offers only Fail and Not assessed on that row and says why under its name. The DS HalalChecklist can’t restrict a row’s options yet (Checks-Gaps).

nD17.text: Scope sufficient (H6) is treated like Issuer accepted (H2): with the scope Specific menu items or Supplier chain only, Pass isn’t offered and only Fail or Not assessed can be recorded. With Whole establishment or Kitchen only, the row suggests Pass. The Fail preselects Scope doesn’t cover this restaurant in Reject. Needs API: the server refuses Scope sufficient (H6) Pass for those scopes (Needs API list, item 6).

nD18.text: Revoke has two branches from account_state. Live (Noor Grill, from the register: Verify-NoorCurrent, the code check, Verify-Revoke): it goes off the app now; orders in progress continue and those customers get an informational notice. Not live yet (Karahi House, from its application: Verify-ApprovedSuper, Shell-StepUp, this board): its application can’t be approved until a new certificate is approved.

nD2.text: Until the transcription is saved, the checks are read-only and Reject is off. Save transcription is the primary button while the transcription is unsaved or changed, and drops to secondary once saved. Any registry body can be saved; only Accepted passes Issuer accepted (H2).

nD3.text: SevenChecks mapping: a check with checked_at empty reads “Not recorded”, nothing selected, with its own Record button. computed_result shows as “Suggested: …” under the name; a result that differs opens the required note (20 or more characters) inside the row. Roll-up words everywhere: recorded, pass, fail, not assessed.

nD4.text: Locks: Dates valid (H5) and Unique, not reused (H7) are computed and locked. Issuer accepted (H2) is locked too whenever the issuing body isn’t Accepted: Pass isn’t offered, only Fail or Not assessed (“HFSAA is Suspended in the registry”). The client enforces it from the payload; the server should refuse it too (Needs API). Each Fail preselects Reject’s reason. None uses red.

nD5.text: When the revoke panel opens its heading takes focus, and Keep it approved is the first button. One sentence from account_state: live (Noor Grill: in-progress orders continue with an informational notice, new orders stop) or not live yet (Karahi House, Verify-RevokeNotLive). Revoke certificate stays off until the box is ticked, and is not the danger variant: red on a halal action reads as a religious ruling.

nD6.text: Reject… is on only when you hold the claim and at least one check is recorded as Fail (a rejection needs a Fail and a reason). Its accessible name otherwise: “Reject…, unavailable: record the check that fails first”. The Fail preselects the reason. Suspected forgery or “the issuer says it wasn’t issued”: record H1 Legible and complete as Fail with a forgery note and release the claim (owner decision, round 2). Only a super admin decides while the hold is on; the page is read-only for reviewers.

nD7.text: An issuer that needs confirmation: Approve stays off until the reviewer records how and when the issuer confirmed the certificate. Needs API: an out-of-band confirmation record on the certificate.

nD8.text: A renewal arrives outside any application, so no application claim applies: Needs API, a review claim on a certificate. It is reached from the register’s Next step. Approving supersedes the current certificate without a gap in the badge.

nD9.text: Reflow (WCAG 1.4.10): at 1280 the panes narrow (scan 360, transcription 340) and nothing else changes. At 200% zoom the panes stack in one column, the SideNav collapses to a menu button and the page scrolls vertically. Nothing scrolls sideways.

nE1.text: Until the API enforces the claim on certificate writes, saving and deciding turn off client-side at review_lock_expires_at from GET application. Tagged on the strip: Needs API, halal-certificate writes require the application review lock.

nE2.text: With no document nothing can be transcribed, checked, approved or rejected. The only action is Ask for a new certificate…, primary, in the decision bar. There is no Reject… on this page.

nE3.text: The Dates valid (H5) 409 (CHECK_NOT_OVERRIDABLE) only comes from a stale page. Its copy is built from details.check_key and details.computed (Fail), and its one action reloads the checks. 422 CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE has its own board, Verify-Incomplete.

nE4.text: The full viewer: page thumbnails, the scan and the transcription rail side by side, 900 tall. At 1280 the rail narrows to 260 and thumbnails to 120; at 200% zoom everything is one column and pages become a row of 44px buttons. Only the scan region pans; the page never scrolls sideways.

nG1.text: Blocking alerts are role=alert with tabindex -1 and take focus when they appear. All others are role=status and never move focus.

nG2.text: Shell-Focus captures the real Button, IconButton, Select and Checkbox. The recompiled tokens.css sets the focus ring to brand 600 (brand 400 in dark), with the ring, offset and field-border widths, so no local focus or font overrides remain on this canvas.

nG3.text: Annotations live outside component bodies. Strip badge: bound only to profile.halal.display_state through HalalState; a missing value renders no badge, loading shows a skeleton. Transcription: issuing body options come from GET /v1/admin/halal-issuing-bodies, every status. Checks: the suggestion comes from computed_result. Decision bar names: “Approve…, unavailable: H6 Scope sufficient is recorded as Fail”; “Reject…, unavailable: record the check that fails first”.

nG5.text: Needs API list (this canvas, new or widened): 1) halal-certificate writes require the application review lock (409 REVIEW_LOCK_LOST on transcription, checks and decision); pairs with 2) a review claim on a certificate outside an application (renewals). 3) Issuer accepted (H2) can’t be recorded as Pass when the issuing body isn’t Accepted. 4) an accept-invite endpoint returning an enrolment-only session (staff invites and authenticator enrolment move to launch: owner decision, round 2). 5) the minimum remaining validity readable by the console. 6) the server refuses Scope sufficient (H6) Pass when the scope is Specific menu items or Supplier chain only. 7) an enrolment response without recovery codes. 8) a super admin resets a staff member’s password or authenticator after calling them back on the phone number on file and matching two account details; a phone number on staff accounts. 9) request a new renewal certificate from a live restaurant (the renewal stays open, the current certificate stays in place). 10) a “waiting on certifying body” application state, and releasing the claim. 11) change or remove a menu item on a restaurant’s behalf. 12) reviewed change requests on the restaurant profile (description, display name, legal name, address, GST/HST number). 13) the restaurant name and the live version on each pending menu version.

nH1.text: Noor Grill’s current certificate HMA-ON-2025-0981 is reached from its register row and from the renewal’s “See the current certificate”. Medina Bakery has no board on this canvas, so its row carries no link rather than another restaurant’s record.

nH2.text: Expiring soon now shows the amber tint in the Restaurant now column and the strips, labelled “Halal certified · expires 19 Oct” (owner decisions). The Expires column shows the short date; the tooltip, open on Noor Grill’s row, and screen readers get the full date.

nI1.text: Only super admins accept, reject, suspend, retire or reinstate a body, each with a justification of at least 20 characters. Admins read the list. Support agents see name and status only. Review… opens the in-page panel beside the grid. Owner decision (round 2): while a super admin decides on a proposed body, the reviewer releases the claim and the application waits on the certifying body (Verify-WaitingOnBody); once the body is accepted or rejected it comes back at the top of the queue.

nL1.text: Layout rules (owner, all admin canvases). Every working page is 1440×900 and never scrolls. Panes sit side by side, overview to detail to more detail (list, application, document; scan, transcription, checks), and resize from keyboard-focusable separators (proposed: SplitPanes). Long lists virtualise inside their own grid. Detail and decisions open in in-page panels that appear only when needed, never modals or sheets. The navigation collapses to a rail on detail pages. Two exceptions: session expired stays a blocking sign-in dialog (it is not a working task), and at 200% zoom the panes stack and the page scrolls vertically, because reflow comes first.

nP1.text: Proposed components here, built only from DS parts or shadcn/ui, for owner approval: SplitPanes (shadcn Resizable, with the 48px collapsed strip); DetailPanel (the in-page decision panel); SevenChecks (all seven checks in one view, see Checks-Gaps); HalalBadge expiring state (HalalState, until the DS HalalBadge draws the amber tint); DateCell (short date, full date in a Tooltip); LyteNyte grid; FilterBar; EmptyState; InlineAlert; Textarea; DocumentViewer; Wordmark; IconButton onColor. Approved for the design system, not in the library yet: SideNav (now also collapsible) and KeyValueList.

nQ1.text: Owner decisions applied here. Staff get no recovery codes: a lost authenticator is reset only by a super admin, who calls the person back on the phone number on file and matches two account details (SignIn-Help). A forgotten password is reset by the staff member from an emailed link (SignIn-Forgot). An expiring-soon certificate shows the amber tint everywhere (HalalState). Table cells use the short date; the tooltip and the detail views use the full date. Round 2: password reset, staff invites and authenticator enrolment, Staff and the menu review queue move to launch; My sessions stays a later version. Expiring soon reads “Halal certified · expires 20 Oct”. Times are 12-hour. The recompiled design-system tokens replaced every local override.

nRNF.text: Removed earlier: “Reject with no recorded Fail”. It contradicted the rule that a rejection needs at least one Fail and a reason. Needs owner decision: reject without a recorded Fail. Until then, Reject… stays off until a check is recorded as Fail.

rowC.text: Application: list, application, documents and scan in panes; decisions in an in-page panel

rowM.text: Menu reviews and restaurant profile changes

nM1.text:
Owner decisions applied here (round 2).

Restaurants edit their own menus at launch, so the menu review queue ships too: listMenuReviewQueue and decideMenuVersion, which the contract still marks a later version. Only words, photos and dietary and allergen tags wait; price and availability change at once. A claim-bearing field is never approved by silence.

Admins can also change or remove an item on a restaurant’s behalf (a new admin operation, Needs API); their edits go live on save and are recorded with their name.

A restaurant’s description, display name and GST/HST number go through a reviewed change request, like legal name and address. Profile changes is that queue; every part of it is Needs API, because today submitRestaurantProfile applies changes at once.
